per_call.title: Python packages, median time of one call

footnotes.text: pgmpy runs a random-forest Pillai test. FastCIT runs a linear Pillai test. The two tests differ.
pgmpy and gcastle apply the Yates correction on 2 × 2 tables and cannot turn it off. FastCIT runs without it.
Different null approximation or kernel width rule from FastCIT.

The time does not include the one-time setup. FastCIT and causal-learn precompute the correlation matrix. FastCIT computes it in the first call and keeps it. The other packages in these rows compute it in every call. The total-time tables in [summary.md](https://github.com/pgmpy/FastCIT/blob/main/benchmarks/results/summary.md) include the setup.

The engine raised an error or returned NaN on some queries. [summary.md](https://github.com/pgmpy/FastCIT/blob/main/benchmarks/results/summary.md) lists them. The median uses only the queries with a result. Those queries can cost less or more than the excluded ones. Compare such a cell with care.

total_per_pass.title: Python packages, total time of one pass
total_per_pass.note: Each pass builds the state of the engine (data conversion, test object, correlation matrix). Then it runs all queries of the group once. Each run keeps its fastest of 5 passes. The table shows the median of the 3 run values.

per_call.title: R packages, median time of one call

footnotes.text: Different null approximation or kernel width rule from FastCIT.

The time does not include the one-time setup. FastCIT and pcalg precompute the correlation matrix. FastCIT computes it in the first call and keeps it. bnlearn and ppcor compute it in every call. The total-time tables in [summary.md](https://github.com/pgmpy/FastCIT/blob/main/benchmarks/results/summary.md) include the setup.
Uses the nominal degrees of freedom. FastCIT uses the adjusted degrees of freedom.
bnlearn ci.test() checks the whole data frame in each call. The benchmark gives it only the columns of the query.
ppcor needs at least one conditioning variable. For a query with an empty set, the benchmark calls stats::cor.test, which runs the same t-test.

The engine raised an error or returned NaN on some queries. [summary.md](https://github.com/pgmpy/FastCIT/blob/main/benchmarks/results/summary.md) lists them. The median uses only the queries with a result. Those queries can cost less or more than the excluded ones. Compare such a cell with care.
